components.name: Bento Cell
components.description: The grid unit. Its span states how real the thing is — the feature cell is 2x2 because it is the only project actually running.
components.html:
Studying

Value investing

Financial Markets, Yale University via Coursera.
components.css: .ds-cell { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: .75rem; padding: 1.5rem; border: 1px solid #26262E; border-radius: 22px; background: #141419; color: #F2F2F5; overflow: hidden; transition: border-color .3s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-cell:hover { border-color: #34343E; } .ds-cell h3 { margin: 0; font: 700 1.1875rem/1.25 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.025em; padding-right: 5.5rem; } .ds-cell p { margin: 0; color: #9B9BA6; font-size: .9375rem; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pinned to the cell's top-right corner. Never stacked above a heading — a label above a title is an eyebrow, and this system does not use them.
components.css: .ds-tag { position: absolute; top: 1.5rem; right: 1.5rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: .4em; padding: .3em .6em; border: 1px solid #34343E; border-radius: 999px; background: #1B1B21; font: 500 .6875rem/1 'Geist Mono', monospace; color: #9B9BA6; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-tag-live { color: #E8A63C; border-color: rgba(232,166,60,.45); } .ds-tag-live::before { content: ""; width: .38em; height: .38em; border-radius: 50%; background: #E8A63C; }

components.name: Accent Button
components.description: The single page action, pinned top right in the nav and repeated at the foot of the contact form.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: .5rem; padding: .6rem 1.1rem; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: #E8A63C; color: #17120A; font: 600 .875rem/1 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.01em; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 6px 18px -8px rgba(232,166,60,.7); transition: transform .2s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), background .2s; } .ds-btn:hover { background: #F2BC63; transform: translateY(-1px); }

components.name: Grain Layer
components.description: Runtime-generated noise tile animated by transform only. The same tile reads as light bloom on black and paper tooth on white.
components.css: .ds-grain { position: fixed; top: -60%; left: -60%; width: 220%; height: 220%; z-index: 100; pointer-events: none; opacity: .085; mix-blend-mode: overlay; background-repeat: repeat; will-change: transform; animation: ds-grain 7s steps(1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-grain { 0%,100% { transform: translate(0,0); } 25% { transform: translate(.9%,-1.4%); } 50% { transform: translate(1.4%,.7%); } 75% { transform: translate(1.1%,-1.1%); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-grain { animation: none; } }

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: Circular icon button beside the CTA. The theme is applied by an inline head script before first paint so there is no flash of the wrong theme.
components.html: <button class="ds-toggle" type="button" aria-label="Switch to light theme"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.2"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-toggle { width: 2.25rem; height: 2.25rem; display: grid; place-items: center; border: 1px solid #26262E; border-radius: 50%; background: transparent; color: #9B9BA6; cursor: pointer; transition: color .2s, border-color .2s, background .2s; } .ds-toggle:hover { color: #F2F2F5; border-color: #34343E; background: #141419; } .ds-toggle svg { width: 1rem; height: 1rem; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.7; stroke-linecap: round; }

narrative.overview: The page is dark by default and grain-lit throughout, and the visitor can flip it to paper. Both grounds are real designs rather than a filter over one another: each has its own surface ladder, border weights, and accent value. The organising idea is that size is the argument — the work sits in a bento of deliberately unequal cells, and the sizing is the honest claim. Hanzi Mind is the only thing actually running, so it occupies four times the area of a plan; coursework gets a small square. Nothing has to say which item is more real, because the grid already did. Typography is minimal and set hard, and there is exactly one hue on the page: an amber carried over from the subject's existing brand that survives the theme flip, which is what keeps a two-theme site from feeling like two sites.
keyCharacteristics: Cell size encodes how real the work is — remove the hierarchy and the page starts lying
Two complete themes, not one theme with a filter over it
One hue only; the accent's fill is shared across themes, its text value is not
Grain is a real generated layer animated by transform, never a texture screenshot
Status lives in a corner badge, because this system has no eyebrows

rules.name: Size Is The Argument
rules.body: Bento spans are assigned by how real the thing is, not by composition. The only running project is 2x2; plans and coursework are 1x1. Any new cell must earn its span the same way.

rules.name: The Accent Has Two Values
rules.body: --accent (#E8A63C) is the fill and is identical in both themes. --accent-tx is the text value and must change: #E8A63C is 9.1:1 on near-black but 2.3:1 on paper, so light drops to #8F5B08 at 5.2:1.

rules.name: One Hue
rules.body: Amber is the only brand hue. The three chart colours are a categorical data series confined to the language composition bar and must not leak into UI chrome.

rules.name: Mono Means Measured
rules.body: Geist Mono is for years, specs, labels, badges and field names. Schibsted Grotesk is for anything a person wrote. Mono is never used to make prose look technical.

rules.name: No Eyebrows
rules.body: Status is a badge pinned to a corner, never a label stacked above a heading. Headings reserve a right-hand gutter so the two cannot collide.

rules.name: Theme Before Paint
rules.body: An inline script in <head> writes data-theme before first paint. Any future theme work must preserve that ordering or the page flashes the wrong ground.

rules.name: Grain Is Atmosphere
rules.body: Keep the grain layer at or below .1 opacity and animate transform only. Above that it reads as dirt, and animating anything else forces a repaint every frame.

dos: Do size bento cells by how real the thing is
Do pick the accent's text value from the active theme
Do put status in a corner badge, never above a heading
Do gate motion behind prefers-reduced-motion and keep revealed content visible by default
Do draw icons as SVG at stroke-width 1.7 with round caps
donts: Don't add shadow to create hierarchy — use surface level and border weight
Don't nest cards inside bento cells
Don't state anything the product record does not confirm; the cell statuses are load-bearing
Don't let the grain go above .1 opacity
